cd2030.core is the Countdown to 2030 analysis of routine health facility data. This guide loads a dataset, looks at
its quality, computes coverage and saves the work, in about twenty lines of R. Each step has its own guide with the
detail:

| Step | Guide |
|---|---|
| What a dataset file must contain | `vignette("preparing-data")` |
| Reporting rates, outliers, missing values, consistency | `vignette("data-quality")` |
| Adjustment, denominators, coverage, reports | `vignette("coverage")` |
| The Shiny apps built on this package | `vignette("building-an-app")` |

## Install

The package is published on r-universe, not CRAN. datasuite.ui, which it needs, is in the same repository.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(
  "cd2030.core",
  repos = c("https://damurka.r-universe.dev", "https://alkemalab.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)
```

Add `dependencies = TRUE` for the optional features: PDF and PowerPoint export, and the Bayesian coverage model.

## Load a dataset

A dataset is the Countdown Excel workbook, a Stata `.dta` master file, or an `.rds` saved by this package. The
package comes with an example workbook for Kenya.

```{r}
library(cd2030.core)

path <- system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core")
cache <- load_cache_data(path)
```

Loading reads the sheets, cleans the column names, merges them into one table with a row per district and month, and
works out which indicator group the file holds (`"rmncah"` or `"vaccine"`). It also names the columns that are empty.

`cache` is a `CacheConnection`: the data together with every choice made about it (years removed, adjustment
factors, denominators, surveys). The data itself is a tibble of class `cd_data`.

```{r}
data <- cache$countdown_data
data
```

For the country it found, the package fills in the reference data it holds: UN population estimates, WUENIC
immunization estimates and the household surveys.

```{r}
cache$country
cache$survey_years
```

If you only want the data, `load_data(path)` returns the `cd_data` tibble without the `CacheConnection`.

## Look at the quality of the data

The quality functions take the data and return a table. Most take an administrative level: `"national"`,
`"adminlevel_1"` (region) or `"district"`.

```{r}
calculate_average_reporting_rate(data)
```

Most results have a `plot()` method.

```{r}
plot(calculate_district_reporting_rate(data, threshold = 90))
```

`calculate_overall_score()` puts the checks in one table: completeness, extreme outliers, consistency between
related indicators, and a score for each year.

```{r}
calculate_overall_score(data, threshold = 90)[, c("no", "Data Quality Metrics", "2022", "2023")]
```

## Adjust the data and compute coverage

Coverage is computed from adjusted data: counts scaled up for incomplete reporting, with extreme outliers and
missing values replaced. The `CacheConnection` does this with the settings it holds and keeps the result.

```{r}
cache$set_k_factors(c(anc = 0.25, idelv = 0.25, vacc = 0.25, opd = 0.25, ipd = 0.25))
cache$adjust_data()
```

Coverage also needs a few national rates. Those the country's latest survey has are already filled in; this
survey has no stillbirth rate, so it is given here.

```{r}
cache$set_national_estimates(list(sbr = 0.02))

coverage <- cache$get_filtered_coverage("penta3", "national")
coverage
```

The table sets the facility-data estimate beside the survey and WUENIC estimates, and so does its chart.

```{r}
plot(coverage)
```

## Save the work

Give the dataset a path and it saves itself there, now and after each later change. `load_cache_data()` opens the
file again with every choice as it was.

```{r}
saved <- file.path(tempdir(), "kenya.rds")
cache$set_cache_path(saved)

reopened <- load_cache_data(saved)
reopened$k_factors
```

## Where to go next

- `vignette("preparing-data")` describes the workbook and how to check your own file.
- `vignette("data-quality")` and `vignette("coverage")` follow the analysis step by step.
- The reference lists every function by analysis step. `?CacheConnection` lists everything the dataset object holds
  and computes.
- The same analysis is available without writing R in the Countdown apps (cd2030.rmncah, cd2030.vaxx), which run
  inside DataSuite. `vignette("building-an-app")` describes how they are built.
